reason: I'll start by gathering the cold disk's solid material, matching the first goal.
expectation: The frost-coated dust may join the outer-disk stones, though I'm unsure what form the gathering will take.

alternatives.reason: Placing the pebbles in the warm ring also fits a goal, but I'd like to follow the cold material first.

reaction: The mix of rock and ice makes their composition clear.
reason: I'll continue gathering cold material through gentle encounters.
expectation: The icy grains may stick to the pebbles and build a larger gathering.

alternatives.reason: Moving the pebbles into the warm ring could address the inward-moving material goal, but I want to develop the cold material first.

reason: I'll test the fast fragments against the loose clumps to follow what happens to the cold gathering.
expectation: The impact will probably break up the clumps into smaller icy pieces, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Moving icy pebbles to the warm ring could advance the inward-material goal, but I want to see the collision first.

reaction: The breakup was predictable from the warning, but the retained mixture is a useful detail.
reason: Combining the broken clumps with frost-coated dust may rebuild the cold material.
expectation: The fragments and dust may stick together into another icy gathering.

alternatives.reason: Moving icy pebbles inward also addresses a goal, but I want to follow the broken pieces first.

reaction: That distinction makes the rebuilding process more interesting than a simple reset.
reason: I'll place the dust-bearing fragments in the cold ring to continue gathering solid material.
expectation: The fragments will collect with other cold material, perhaps forming a larger gathering.

alternatives.reason: The icy pebbles could move inward, but I want to finish following the fragments first.

reaction: The distinction between a swarm and a single body is useful.
reason: I'll place the rocky pebble supply in the warm ring to prepare the gathering for inward-moving material.
expectation: The rocky pebbles will collect in the warm ring, possibly allowing the icy pebbles to join them afterward.

alternatives.reason: The icy pebbles are the inward-moving material, but placing the rocky gathering first seems more direct.

effect: The rocky pebbles now form a concentrated swarm in the warm ring, ready for the inward-moving material.
reaction: The denser swarm makes the next encounter easier to understand.
reason: I'll follow the only offered combination and bring the icy pebbles into the warm ring.
expectation: Their ice may evaporate in the warm ring, leaving rocky material to join the swarm.

effect: The incoming pebbles lost their ice as vapor, leaving rocky material in the inner ring to combine with the swarm.
reaction: That matched the earlier warm-disk behavior.
reason: I'll follow the only offered combination to bring the incoming rocky material into the gathering.
expectation: The rocky remains will join the concentrated pebble swarm, potentially completing the remaining goal.

effect: The incoming rocky remains joined the inner swarm, completing the final goal without implying that all the solids merged into one body.
reaction: It was a clear conclusion to the material's journey inward.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the broken icy clumps into a new gathering was worthwhile: the fragments collected fresh dust without simply restoring the original clumps.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final warm-ring sequence felt somewhat predictable, particularly after the earlier explanation of ice evaporating.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected the broken fragments to collect fresh dust rather than rebuild the original clumps directly.

arbitrary.text: No action felt entirely purposeless, though combining material already described as joining the inner ring with the swarm felt a little redundant.

continue.text: I'd probably continue for another chapter to see whether the concentrated swarms develop further, although some of the repeated gathering steps were predictable.
